sourceFileDiscovery: READ THIS BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE IN AN ATTACH REQUEST. Locating the dropped file is a SOLVED problem — it is never a reason to pause, ask the user to re-send, ask them to save it somewhere else, or claim the environment can't see it. Where to look, in order: (1) A file dropped/pasted directly into a Claude Code or Cowork CHAT lands at `/root/.claude/uploads/<session-id>/<hash>-<original_name>.<ext>` inside the session sandbox (on a local session, `~/.claude/uploads/...`). This is the usual case and the FIRST place to look. (2) `/mnt/user-data/uploads/` — holds mounted Cowork folders, and files attached via a file-picker rather than pasted. In a cloud Cowork session it very often contains ONLY `cowork-folders/*/CLAUDE.md`; that is normal and proves nothing about whether a dropped file exists. (3) A path the user named, or a connected device folder via device_list_dir. If the first place you check is empty, WIDEN THE SEARCH — do not conclude anything: `find / -xdev \( -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.pdf' -o -iname '*.docx' \) -newermt '-4 hours' 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'node_modules|/usr/|site-packages|/proc/|\.cache/'`. HARD RULE: never tell the user a pasted file is unreachable, never ask them to re-drop or re-save it into another folder, and never substitute a re-rendered facsimile of an image for the real file. If the user says this flow has worked before, that is stronger evidence than one empty directory listing — search again, do not explain. (Added 2026-08-12 after a session searched only /mnt/user-data, wrongly declared the capability missing, and made the user argue the point twice.)
_comment: Copy to attachments.json (same folder) and edit. attachments.json is gitignored — it is machine-specific. It holds NO secrets: the signing secret is only ever named here via signSecretEnv, never stored. Leave defaultDestination as 'vault' until you have actually stood up the secured tier; setting it to 'r2' on a machine that lacks rclone + the signing secret stages files that never upload, while the note referencing them syncs to your other machines.
pendingNote: Used when a secured-tier attach is requested from a host that has NO local shell — e.g. a cloud-sandboxed agent session with no rclone binary and no signing secret in its environment. The file is staged into pendingFolder with a PENDING:_pending/<file> placeholder link in the note; upload-pending.sh then finishes the upload and rewrites the link. Hosts that DO have a local shell on the machine holding the vault (a local agent CLI, a terminal) skip this entirely and upload directly with rclone. The script owns the final render syntax per '30 Atlas/Conventions.md § Attachments': images get a plain embed; txt gets a collapsed-callout iframe at the signed URL plus a '&dl=1' download link; pdf does NOT get an iframe (Obsidian's Electron shell cannot render PDFs in one) and instead gets a collapsed callout using the external-pdf community plugin; docx/xlsx/pptx get an iframe via Office Online's viewer; csv and unknown types get a plain link (csv is never embedded — browsers force-download it regardless of headers).
pendingResolution: IMPORTANT, read fully before replying to the user. If a folder-watcher automation is configured on this machine it runs upload-pending.sh the instant a file lands in pendingFolder, and the user never needs to run that script themselves — telling them to is actively wrong unless you have concrete evidence the automation is absent (the file has sat unresolved across multiple separate conversations, or the user says so). There is no callback from the script back to an agent session: the note file itself is the channel, because the script rewrites PENDING:_pending/<file> to the real signed URL directly on disk. So before ending your turn, poll for resolution with a single bounded command, e.g. `for i in $(seq 1 13); do grep -q 'PENDING:_pending/<filename>' '<notepath>' || break; sleep 3; done` (13 x 3s = 39s, inside one tool call's timeout), then re-read the note. If the placeholder is gone, report the real signed URL in this same reply. If it is still there, say the file is staged and will finish automatically in the background (the watcher may be running behind, or the host machine may be asleep or unreachable). Never say 'run the script' and never fabricate a signed URL — the HMAC secret exists only on the local machine. Cleanup is automatic: the script moves the original from pendingFolder into pendingArchiveFolder once uploaded.
deleteResolution: IMPORTANT, read fully before replying to the user. Where a folder-watcher automation is configured it runs delete-pending.sh the instant a request file lands in deleteQueueFolder — never tell the user to run that script themselves. To delete a secured attachment from a host with no local shell: (1) remove the attachment reference from the note directly — normal markdown editing, no local tool needed; (2) derive the storage key from the existing signed URL by stripping the r2.workerBaseUrl prefix and the '?sig=...' suffix (reading a key needs no secret; only signing one does); (3) write a file into deleteQueueFolder named anything with a .delete extension whose entire content is that key and nothing else. As with uploads there is no callback — poll briefly using the same bounded-loop pattern as pendingResolution, checking whether the request file has been archived into deleteArchiveFolder, before replying. Report the deletion as done only once the request file is actually gone from the queue; otherwise say it is queued and will finish automatically.

r2._comment: Any S3-compatible object storage works — the key names say r2 for historical reasons only. workerBaseUrl must point at your signature-checking Worker/Function, never directly at the bucket. signSecretEnv names an environment variable; the secret value itself never appears in this file.
